title: Formalize per-endpoint degradation contracts, token escrow accounting, and regional rescue protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Define a formal per-endpoint "degradation contract" that ties SLI definitions (availability, latency, quality) to a token-aware error budget ledger, automated burn-rate actions (graded), circuit hysteresis tuning, and a multi-region rescue protocol. The contract will be declarative and attachable to model endpoints and route variants so runtime orchestration can automate shedding, failover, and region ejection decisions.

Motivation: Recent incidents showed ambiguity in when to preempt low-priority traffic versus eject a region. We need a single source of truth for: (1) how we measure request quality for each endpoint, (2) how we account token-sensitive error budget burn for bursts and long-tail latency, and (3) the precise automated actions at burn thresholds (soft shedding, canary holds, regional rescue).

Goals:
- Provide per-endpoint SLI schema covering availability (2xx success rate), latency quantiles, and quality (prompt-suite pass rate).
- Design a token-escrow accounting model that attributes error budget consumption proportionally to tokens and route priority.
- Specify burn-rate thresholds and deterministic automated actions with hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- Define a regional rescue choreography (progressive traffic shift, warmed rescue pool, and rollback criteria).
- Deliver a rollout plan, instrumentation checklist, and runbook snippets for on-call.

Non-Goals: Full implementation of orchestration hooks (separate task). This ticket produces the contract, runbook, metrics spec, and prototype gating rules for the autoscaler/orchestrator to implement.
acceptance_criteria: Documented SLI definitions for chat/generation, embeddings, and reranking routes
Token-escrow ledger design that maps token units to error-budget consumption in examples
Clear burn-rate thresholds with corresponding automated actions (soft-shed, canary-hold, region-eject) and hysteresis parameters
Instrumentation spec listing metrics and labels required for enforcement and alerting
Runbook with step-by-step guidance for manual override and rollback

implementation_notes: Deliver a YAML schema for endpoint contracts: fields: slis[], error_budget_window, token_weighting, priority_buckets
Add enforcement hooks: orchestrator must accept contract and return action decisions (NOOP, SOFT_SHED, CANARY_HOLD, REGION_EJECT)
Instrument metrics: request_count, error_count(4xx/5xx), latency_p50/p95/p99, token_count, quality_failures, kv_cache_hit_rate; label by region/model_variant/route/tenant_tier
Prototype: implement enforcement stub in dev cluster router that logs decisions to 'resilience-decisions' topic for 2 weeks before auto-enforcing
Expose customer signal: console banner + webhook event 'degradation.notice' when soft-shedding thresholds are reached
decision_log: SLI choices: availability measured as successful response (HTTP 200 + model executed) over sliding 30d window; latency SLOs vary by route type (chat p95 <= 300ms target for hosted; embeddings p95 <= 120ms); quality SLO defined as pass-rate of curated prompt-suite per model (>= 95% for GA).
Token accounting: weigh error budget burns by tokens_requested + tokens_generated. Background jobs (bulk embeddings) are assigned lower priority and higher burn multiplier by default.

Burn thresholds: burn_rate >= 3x for 10m => trigger SOFT_SHED of lowest-priority buckets; burn_rate >= 8x for 5m => CANARY_HOLD (freeze rollouts and shove new traffic to rescue pool); burn_rate >= 20x for 2m => REGION_EJECT (automated cutover to rescue pool with progressive traffic shift).
Hysteresis: cooldown 10m after action; half-open probe sends 1% of traffic to previously-ejected region for 5m to verify recovery before full reintegration.

Circuit behavior: circuits are weighted by tenant priority; opening a circuit drops lower-priority traffic first while preserving warm KV cache entries for active sessions to minimize quality regression.
